ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Disposition after aspiration

An 18-year-old improves after peritonsillar abscess drainage. He has no stridor, tolerates oral fluids and medications, has stable vital signs, and has reliable follow-up. Which finding would instead most strongly favor hospital admission?

  1. Persistent inability to swallow fluids
  2. Mild residual odynophagia while drinking adequately
  3. Persistent tonsillar erythema with improving vital signs
  4. Tender cervical nodes without progressive swelling
  5. A throat culture still pending after empiric therapy
Answer and explanation

Persistent inability to swallow fluids

Persistent inability to drink creates a hydration and medication-delivery problem requiring continued supervised care.

Option explanations

Persistent inability to swallow fluids: Persistent inability to drink creates a hydration and medication-delivery problem requiring continued supervised care.

Mild residual odynophagia while drinking adequately: Some residual discomfort is expected and does not itself require admission if hydration and medication intake are adequate.

Persistent tonsillar erythema with improving vital signs: Local inflammation may resolve gradually; improving function and physiology support outpatient care.

Tender cervical nodes without progressive swelling: Reactive nodes can persist and are not by themselves a reason for admission.

A throat culture still pending after empiric therapy: A pending culture alone does not require admission when the patient is otherwise suitable for outpatient care.
